assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organization as phase behaviour of macromolecules: liquid-liquid demixing, wetting, viscoelasticity and ageing now sit at the core of cell biology. This is thermodynamics and soft-matter physics applied to the cell, a genuinely new concept of molecular organisation with broad influence on neurodegeneration and amyloid research, close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 P granule work (Brangwynne, Hyman and colleagues) established liquid-like behaviour in vivo, with Hyman as the senior intellectual driver. Rosen, Pappu and Mittag made decisive theoretical and in vitro contributions on multivalency and sequence grammar, so a two-person prize would leave out important credit. I consider Hyman and Brangwynne the most defensible pair; this is from my own knowledge and I have not verified details.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across hundreds of labs and systems and now textbook-level; the field is still debating how general it is and which condensates have function in vivo, but the central concept is stable. Timing looks right.
uncertainties: Whether the field would regard the prize as chemistry or physiology/medicine
Unsettled role of condensates in vivo versus in vitro artefacts
Fair credit for Rosen, Pappu and Mittag

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly and colloid problem solved by design: pH-dependent charge, controlled nanostructure and fusogenic behaviour enabled in vivo delivery of siRNA and mRNA and underpinned the COVID-19 vaccines. Major real-world impact grounded in lipid physical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and Hope's group developed the early lipid nanoparticle formulation and ionizable lipid concept; Anderson and Langer developed lipid libraries and delivery systems. Credit is spread and overlaps with the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification; I choose Cullis and Hope as the formulation originators, subject to my uncertain recall of who did what.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale; mechanisms of endosomal escape and structure remain refined but the technology is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize
Complex, contested allocation of credit among lipid and formulation groups
Whether the prize reads as chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave a statistical-mechanical framework for protein folding that links thermodynamics, kinetics and evolution. It exemplifies reducing biological complexity to general physical-chemical principles.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic developed funnel and landscape theory; Dill introduced the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model picture; Fersht provided experimental phi-value mapping. A theory-led trio is defensible, though the experimental side has a strong claim.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are long established and widely used; however, AlphaFold-era prediction (2024 prize) may reduce the sense of unmet recognition, and the theory is partly conceptual rather than predictive.
uncertainties: Interaction with the 2024 prize on structure prediction
Choice between theory and experimental contributors
Age and availability of the proposed laureates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials deliver near quantum accuracy at force-field cost, enabling simulations of phase behaviour, interfaces and reactions at scales earlier impossible. Highly consequential for soft matter and materials simulation.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello's 2007 neural-network potential and Bartók, Csányi and colleagues' Gaussian approximation potentials are the two foundational lines. Parrinello is also credited on other candidates, which complicates the allocation. Weinan E and von Lilienfeld are important but later.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly spreading with strong independent adoption, but the field is still evolving quickly and foundation-model approaches may change what is seen as decisive; possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Timing and ongoing methodological change
Overlap of Parrinello with the metadynamics and Car-Parrinello candidates
Complex allocation among several groups

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling became a routine tool for making arylamines in pharmaceuticals and materials and is among the most widely used reactions in synthesis. Impact is clear, though outside my own area.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed general catalysts and the mechanistic basis, building on Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work. The two-person credit is fairly clean, with the Kosugi precedent a possible complication.
assessment.maturity: Mature for decades with extensive industrial use. Follows the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which may reduce urgency, but is timely in terms of lasting impact.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize
Precedent claims such as Kosugi and Migita

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new pharmacological modality, using induced proximity to turn the cellular ubiquitin machinery against chosen proteins. A conceptual change in chemical biology with clinical trials under way.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies proposed and validated PROTACs; Ciulli added the structural and VHL ligand work; the glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) complicates a three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Concept is established but clinical proof is still emerging, so recognition may be early. Independent confirmation is extensive.
uncertainties: Premature if clinical outcomes are not yet decisive
Splitting credit between PROTAC and molecular glue strands
Possible fit with Medicine rather than Chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves noncovalent assemblies in the gas phase, allowing stoichiometry, lipid and ligand binding in membrane protein complexes to be read out. Valuable for studying lipid-protein interactions in my own area.
assessment.attribution: Robinson is the central figure for intact complexes and membrane proteins; Chait and Loo made early and distinct contributions. Heck and Gross are also credited, and mass spectrometry already has several earlier prizes.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely applied, though the 2002 mass spectrometry prize narrows novelty for the technique.
uncertainties: Closeness to earlier ionization prizes
Debated relative contributions of several groups

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a general physical-chemical mechanism underlying biological energy conversion and artificial catalysis, with theory and experiment well integrated.
assessment.attribution: Mayer and Nocera established the experimental PCET framework, while Hammes-Schiffer led theory; Meyer is a pioneering contributor, which makes the credit contested.
assessment.maturity: Concept well confirmed, but the discovery is diffuse across many systems, which weakens its clarity as a single prize topic.
uncertainties: Diffuse definition of the discovery
Allocation between experimentalists, theorists and pioneers like Meyer
